diagram_name: Who Says So? Sorting Claims About Paul
chapter_title: Paul at Ephesus, Part 1: The Apostle's Life, Letters, and Ephesian Years
learning_objective: The learner will differentiate claims about Paul by their source, sorting fourteen statements into Paul's own letters, Acts only, scholars' inference, or later tradition, with at least 11 of 14 correct.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** who-says-so-paul-sources
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Analyze
**Bloom Verb:** differentiate
**Learning Objective:** The learner will differentiate claims about Paul by their source, sorting fourteen statements into Paul's own letters, Acts only, scholars' inference, or later tradition, with at least 11 of 14 correct. **Prerequisites:** primary source and myth versus history (Chapter 4); the Book of Acts, the Pauline letters as Paul's own words, Paul of Tarsus, Paul as persecutor, the road to Damascus, Timothy and Titus, Roman citizenship, and Tarsus (all defined in the chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** The learner places each of 14 statement cards into one of four bins. A placement is correct when it matches the "Correct bin" column in Content. Mastery is 11 of 14 correct on the first attempt. Reading the bin definitions is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) Everything familiar about Paul comes from his letters; in fact his birthplace, his citizenship, the name Saul, and the light on the road come only from Acts. (2) If Acts and the letters both say something, it must be "Acts"; the rule is that Paul's own words come first. (3) Dates such as the year of Paul's call are stated in a source; they are reconstructed by scholars. (4) Paul's death by beheading is in the Bible; it is later tradition. **Instructional Rationale:** Differentiating sources is an Analyze task: the learner must break each familiar claim down to where it comes from. Placing cards one at a time with an immediate reason exposes the most common confusion, that the vivid details of Paul's story are his own, and builds the habit of asking "who says so?" before tomorrow's tour. **Content:** Bins, with the definition shown on each: - **Paul's own letters:** stated in one of the letters scholars agree Paul wrote, whether or not Acts also says it. - **Acts only:** stated in the Book of Acts and not in Paul's letters. - **Scholars' inference:** not stated in any source; reasoned from the evidence. - **Later tradition:** first told by writers after the New Testament. Statement cards, in this fixed order: | # | Statement shown to the learner | Correct bin | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | Paul had been a Pharisee. | Paul's own letters | Paul says "as to the law, a Pharisee" (Philippians 3:5); Acts agrees (Acts 23:6). | | 2 | Paul was born in Tarsus. | Acts only | Only Acts names Tarsus (Acts 22:3); Paul's letters never mention it. | | 3 | Paul was a Roman citizen from birth. | Acts only | Only Acts says so (Acts 22:28); the letters are silent, and some scholars doubt it. | | 4 | Paul also had the Hebrew name Saul. | Acts only | Acts calls him "Saul, who is also called Paul" (Acts 13:9); in his letters he is always Paul. | | 5 | Paul persecuted the followers of Jesus before his call. | Paul's own letters | Paul says he "was violently persecuting the church of God" (Galatians 1:13); Acts agrees. | | 6 | A light from heaven struck Paul to the ground on the road to Damascus. | Acts only | The light and the fall are told in Acts 9, 22, and 26; Paul says only that God revealed his Son to him. | | 7 | After his call, Paul went away into Arabia. | Paul's own letters | Paul mentions Arabia in Galatians 1:17; Acts does not. | | 8 | Paul studied in Jerusalem under the teacher Gamaliel. | Acts only | Only Acts says so (Acts 22:3). | | 9 | Paul supported himself by working with his own hands. | Paul's own letters | Paul says so in 1 Thessalonians 2:9 and 1 Corinthians 4:12; Acts adds that his trade was tentmaking. | | 10 | Titus, a Greek, went to Jerusalem with Paul and was not made to be circumcised. | Paul's own letters | Paul tells this in Galatians 2:1–3; Titus is never named in Acts. | | 11 | Paul was born in the first decade of the 1st century CE. | Scholars' inference | No source gives the year; it is reasoned from Acts calling him a young man and Paul calling himself an old man. | | 12 | Paul's call came between about 33 and 36 CE. | Scholars' inference | No source gives the date; it is reconstructed from the intervals in Galatians 1–2 and the death of King Aretas around 40 CE. | | 13 | Paul was short and bald, with eyebrows that met. | Later tradition | This description comes from the *Acts of Paul and Thecla*, a 2nd-century story. | | 14 | Paul was beheaded in Rome under Nero. | Later tradition | Acts ends with Paul alive under house arrest; the beheading is first told by later Christian writers. | Answer counts: Paul's own letters 5, Acts only 5, Scholars' inference 2, Later tradition 2. **Provenance:** Statements, answers, and verse references come from the chapter sections "Tarsus," "Paul of Tarsus," "Paul as Persecutor," "The Road to Damascus," "Timothy and Titus," "Roman Citizenship," and "Paul's Death in Rome," and from the biblical passages cited. **Rules:** - Each card is correct in exactly one bin, given in Content. - When Paul's letters state a claim, the correct bin is "Paul's own letters" even if Acts also states it. - One attempt per card; a placed card cannot be moved. - Cards appear one at a time in the fixed order. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner reads the four bin definitions. 2. The first card appears; the learner places it in a bin. 3. The feedback for that card appears, and the card stays in the bin the learner chose, marked correct or incorrect; if incorrect, the correct bin is highlighted. 4. The learner continues through all 14 cards. 5. A summary shows the score and the cards grouped by correct bin. 6. The learner should notice that most of the vivid details of the familiar story (Tarsus, citizenship, the name Saul, the light) come from Acts, while the letters give the inner story (Pharisee, persecutor, Arabia, manual work). **Feedback:** Fourteen cards, fixed order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct. [Why]" Incorrect: "This one belongs in [correct bin]. [Why]" For an incorrect placement of cards 1, 5, or 9 into "Acts only," add "Acts says it too, but Paul's own words come first." After card 14: "You sorted [n] of 14 correctly. Mastery is 11." If n < 11, a "Sort again" option clears the bins and restarts from card 1 in the same order. **Starting State:** Four empty labeled bins and the first card, "Paul had been a Pharisee," with the question "Who says so?" **Chapter Anchors:** Four kinds of statement (letters, Acts only, scholars' inference, later tradition); Acts dated about 80–90 CE; Paul's call about 33–36 CE; Aretas IV died around 40 CE; Titus never named in Acts; the *Acts of Paul and Thecla* is 2nd-century; 14 statements.
